prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Baytown, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1068; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision at the intersection in Baytown. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording right now. I'm still dealing with a headache and it's hard to focus.

Q: That's understandable. We can keep it brief. Can you tell me where you were coming from and where you were headed when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light, heading east, on my way home from a job site.

Q: Do you recall the traffic signal being green when you entered the intersection?

A: Yes, I'm fairly sure it was green. I remember watching it as I came up to the crossing.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle came from my right side and hit the driver's side of my car. I didn't see it until just before impact. I braked, but there wasn't time to avoid it.

Q: Did you have any contact with the other vehicle before the impact, or did you swerve?

A: No, I didn't swerve. I was focused on the light and the cars ahead of me.

Q: After the collision, did you feel any injuries?

A: I hit my head on the side window. I had a headache right away, I felt dizzy, and the light bothers my eyes. The doctor said I have a concussion.

Q: Have you been seeing a physician for that?

A: Yes, I've been going in for follow-up visits and I'm resting as much as I can. Some days are better than others.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add that I haven't asked about?

A: Only that I want my car and my medical bills taken care of. I'm still recovering, so I may need to follow up with you later.

Q: Understood. Thank you for your time today. This concludes the statement.
